    • getShowFpQualityNames

      public boolean getShowFpQualityNames()
      Description copied from interface: ICaptureEngineConfig
      gets whether to show the name of the quality "level" for each finger when evaluated. When true, will display the common readable name for the range of quality that the print's quality score falls into. By default, the only quality levels that are defined are for NFIQ1 (the default quality scoring algorithm) where 1=Best, 2=Good, 3=Medium, 4=Poor and 5=Worst. This can be overridden, or other named scoring types can be added by using ICaptureEngineConfigBuilder.addFpInclusiveQualityMapForScoreType(String scoreTypeName, Mapinvalid input: '<'Integer, QualityLevel> map). This defaults to 'false'.
      Specified by:
      getShowFpQualityNames in interface ICaptureEngineConfig
      Returns:
      whether to show the name of the quality "level" for each finger when evaluated

    • getUseQualityLevelColors

      public boolean getUseQualityLevelColors()
      Description copied from interface: ICaptureEngineConfig
      gets whether to use colors during finger review representing the individual QualityLevels of the quality scoring used for validation. If true, then the color representing a print's QualityLevel will be used for its location during review. If false, then the default green/red color scheme will be used based on whether each print passed validation or not. By default the QualityLevel colors are: Best=Green, Good=DarkGreen, Medium=Yellow, Poor=LightRed, Worst=Red. These can be overridden in the application consuming this api by adding color values to the v21\base-colors.xml of the top level application with the names sciometrics_slapshot_finger_quality_level_[best|good|medium|poor|worst]. By default, this is set to 'false'
      Specified by:
      getUseQualityLevelColors in interface ICaptureEngineConfig
      Returns:
      whether to use colors during finger review representing the individual QualityLevels of the quality scoring * used for validation

    • getFpInclusiveQualityMapForScoreTypes

      public Map<String,Map<Integer,QualityLevel>> getFpInclusiveQualityMapForScoreTypes()
      Description copied from interface: ICaptureEngineConfig
      gets the mappings of a quality value threshold to a QualityLevel for a given score type (by the score type's name). The mapping sets the (inclusive) threshold for a given QualityLevel. For example, if a scoring type had a range between [0,100] where a higher score was better, and 5 QualityLevels are wanting to be defined as: QualityLevel.Best=(80,100], QualityLevel.Good=(60,80], QualityLevel.Medium=(40,60], QualityLevel.Poor=(20,40], QualityLevel.Worst=[0,20] then the valid definition of the 'map' would be {{Best,81}, {Good,61}, {Medium,41}, {Poor,21}, {Worst,0}}, such that the thresholds are on the lower, inclusive bounds of the range of the QualityLevel. If a scoring type had a range between [1,10] where a lower score is better and 3 QualityLevels are wanting to be defined as: QualityLevel.Best=[1,3], QualityLevel.Medium=(3,6], QualityLevel.Poor=(6,10], then the valid definition of the 'map' would be {{{Best,3}, {Medium,6}, {Worst,10}}, such that the thresholds are on the upper, inclusive bounds of teh range of the QualityLevel. Not all 5 available QualityLevels need to be represented in the map, nor do the elements need to be in any order. By default, just the levels for the default scoring algorithm (NFIQ1) are set such that QualityLevel.Best=[1,1], QualityLevel.Good=[2,2], QualityLevel.Medium=[3,3], QualityLevel.Poor=[4,4], QualityLevel.Worst=[5,5]. This can be overriden by using addFpInclusiveQualityMapForScoreType("NFIQ",map). are wanting to be defined
      Specified by:
      getFpInclusiveQualityMapForScoreTypes in interface ICaptureEngineConfig
      Returns:
      mappings of a quality value threshold to a QualityLevel for a given score type (by the score type's name).
